State of the MOU
Day 134 of a 60-day clock that expired over two months ago. No status changed: Breached 11, At Risk / Contested 3. Reuters reported on 28 October that Qatar handed Tehran a new draft on 25 October, with a seven-day timetable, daily confidence-building steps and guarantor states, but a senior Iranian official called its terms "unacceptable ideas and not an offer" (contested); Araghchi said Iran is in close contact with intermediaries on its own seven-day plan. Axios, AP and the WSJ reported US and Israeli preparations for days to a week of strikes after the 3 November midterms if diplomacy fails, with Gulf states told to brace for a short, intense campaign; Trump said "anything is possible". The WSJ's report of a Vance letter to Rezaei is unverified and Trump denied directing any outreach. With 88.6% counted in Israel, Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats to the change bloc's 48, and coalition talks have begun. The UN record of the 27 October Council debate shows the agenda adopted 11-2-2 over Russian and Chinese objections and a US proposal for an independent 1737 monitoring mechanism. The Houthi-Saudi war continued: two missiles struck Aden airport and the coalition downed a missile aimed at the Eastern Province early on 29 October. AP reported that Russian satellite targeting data reached the Houthis and Iraqi militias through Iranian advisers. The blockade stays in force, with another carrier group and Patriot systems reported heading to the region. Windward counted 12 Hormuz transits on 27 October, while Gulf crude loadings recovered to about 11m b/d by escorted dark passage (contested). OFAC posted nothing on Iran, and GL FF expires on 30 October. Brent December settled at $115.32 (up $1.44), and the rial held at about 2,702,000 per dollar.
How to refresh: in Cowork, say "update the MOU tracker" — each article is re-checked against the latest reporting (CENTCOM/Treasury/IAEA notices, Reuters/AP/CNN/Al Jazeera, ISW/Soufan analysis) and statuses, evidence logs and the day-counter are updated. This file does not update itself. Sourcing rule: verification uses primary/official records and established press or analysis only — open-edit encyclopedias such as Wikipedia are excluded.
